number.description: A numeric tower: integer -> rational -> real -> complex, each exact or inexact.

boolean.description: `#t` and `#f`. Only `#f` is false — the empty list is true, unlike Lisp.

string.description: A mutable sequence of characters in most implementations; literals may be immutable.

symbol.description: An interned name. Produced by `quote` and compared with `eq?`.

pair.description: A cons cell of `car` and `cdr`; the building block of lists.

list.description: A chain of pairs ending in the empty list `()`. An improper list ends in a non-pair.

procedure.description: A callable closure. First-class and anonymous via `lambda`.

void.description: The void value returned by side-effecting procedures like display and set!

promise.description: A delayed computation from `delay`, forced by `force`.

continuation.description: A first-class procedure representing the rest of the computation, from `call/cc`.
